memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Go to the place the Lord your God will choose as a dwelling for his Name and say to the priest in office at the time, 'I declare today to the Lord your God that I have come to the land the Lord swore to our ancestors to give us.'" — Deut 26:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Worship in Israel was never meant to be vague or forgetful. As the worshipper handed over his basket, he spoke out loud what God had done: the Lord had kept His word and brought them into the land He promised their ancestors. This was worship that remembered.

We forget so easily. When life is comfortable, we quietly begin to believe we built it ourselves. The declaration this Israelite made was a guard against that pride. Standing before the priest, he named God as the giver and himself as the receiver. He located his whole life inside God's faithfulness.

This is a healthy pattern for us too. Real worship is not just feeling something; it is remembering and saying something true about God. When you gather with God's people, when you pray, when you give, it helps to name specifically what God has done — He saved me, He kept me, He provided, He was faithful. Speaking it keeps our hearts honest and grateful.

And every promise God kept for Israel points to the greatest promise kept in Christ, in whom all God's promises find their "Yes" (2 Cor 1:20). We worship a God who has never once broken His word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last put into words what God has actually done for me?
2. Does my worship remember God's faithfulness, or drift into vague feeling?
3. What specific thing can I thank God for by name today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from forgetting all You have done. Help me to name Your faithfulness out loud and to worship You with a remembering heart. Amen.
